name: Vijay Kardak
tagline: I build the pipelines that ship other people's ideas.

story: I started out breaking Linux installs on purpose, just to learn how to fix them. That habit never really went away — it just got a YAML file and a CI pipeline attached to it.

DevOps found me somewhere between a crashed EC2 instance and a Docker container that refused to stop restarting. What kept me here wasn't the tools, it was the idea that reliability is a design decision, not an accident.
I care about systems that fail loudly, recover quietly, and never need a 2 AM phone call twice for the same reason.
about.whyDevOps: Because the interesting part of software was never the last line of code — it was everything that happens after: build, ship, watch, fix, repeat. DevOps is the discipline of making that loop boring, in the best possible way.
about.learningMindset: I learn in public and in production-shaped sandboxes. Every tool on this site got there because I broke it first, then wrote down what fixed it.
goals: Go deep on Kubernetes internals, not just kubectl commands
Get comfortable running GitOps workflows with ArgoCD end to end
Build a home lab that mirrors real production observability stacks
Contribute to an open-source DevOps tool
